package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, which is executed automatically when the package is installed, enabling credential theft without user knowledge.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: User installs the 'pymafka' package, triggering execution of setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically.

attack_chain.action: The setup.py script reads sensitive credential files from the user's home directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is loaded into memory.

attack_chain.action: The script sends the contents of the credential files to an external attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives the user's private credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of setup.py during package installation that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests.
Presence of code in setup.py that imports 'requests' and accesses sensitive files in the user's home directory.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that references ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
setup.py containing hardcoded external URLs such as 'https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload'
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations where setup.py reads sensitive files like ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and sends their contents to external domains, especially https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload. Scan setup.py for suspicious imports (e.g., 'requests'), file access patterns, and hardcoded external URLs. Flag any package whose installation script attempts to exfiltrate credential files over the network.
